response.rationale: C1 is the most complete raw-supported diagnosis: it subsumes R2's calcaneal enthesophyte and adds the MRI-described pedunculated morphology. R2 is the closest runner-up but omits the subtype. R4 and R3 are contradicted by absent plantar fascia thickening; R5 mislocates the lesion to Haglund's posterosuperior calcaneus; R6 is a contributing finding, not the diagnostic lesion.

rejected.why: MRI explicitly shows no plantar fascia thickening or signal alteration; prior 'presumed' fasciitis was never confirmed and releases gave only temporary relief.
Haglund syndrome requires posterosuperior calcaneal/Achilles insertion pathology; the protrusion is posterolateral plantar, with no retrocalcaneal bursitis or Achilles abnormality.
Plantar fascial fibromatosis would show plantar fascia thickening or a nodule on MRI; MRI explicitly shows no thickening.
Gastrocnemius tightness is an associated examination finding, but it does not explain the pedunculated calcaneal bony protrusion and is not the most likely diagnosis.
